JSON value.\n    pub fn to_data(&self) -> serde_json::Value {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": cycle_count,\n                    \"last_strand_evaluated\": last_strand,\n                    \"waterfall_restarts\": waterfall_restarts,\n                    \"restart_triggers\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepCompleted { step, duration_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step, \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                deferred_count,\n                total_wait_secs,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"deferred_count\": deferred_count,\n                    \"total_wait_secs\": total_wait_secs,\n                    \"reason\": reason\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                strand_name,\n                result,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"result\": result,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                strand_name,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"strand_name\": strand_name, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadStoreError {\n                strand_name,\n                operation,\n                error_message,\n                stderr,\n                exit_code,\n                workspace,\n            } => {\n                let mut data = serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"operation\": operation,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"stderr\": stderr,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                });\n                if let Some(ws) = workspace {\n                    if let Some(obj) = data.as_object_mut() {\n                        obj.insert(\"workspace\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(ws));\n                    }\n                }\n                data\n            }\n            EventKind::QueueEmpty => serde_json::json!({}),\n            EventKind::PluckStarvationDetected {\n                workspace,\n                open_count,\n                excluded_count,\n                candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"workspace\": workspace,\n                    \"open_count\": open_count,\n                    \"excluded_count\": excluded_count,\n                    \"candidate_exclusion_reasons\": candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimAttempt { bead_id, attempt } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"attempt\": attempt })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                bead_id,\n                priority,\n                strand,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"priority\": priority,\n                    \"strand\": strand,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLost { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLostSkipped {\n                consecutive_losses,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"consecutive_losses\": consecutive_losses,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleased { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                duration_ms,\n            }      }\n            EventKind::RoutingDecision {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                matched_rule,\n                chosen_adapter,\n            } => {\n \"chosen_adapter\": chosen_adapter,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RoutingFailed {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                rules_tried,\n EventKind::BuildHeartbeat {\n                bead_id,\n                elapsed_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::OutcomeClassified {\n                bead_id,\n                outcome,\n                exit_code,\n A gate that cannot pass is not\n426\t        // a gate; it is an outage with a good reputation.\n427\t        let canary_timeout = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_global()\n428\t            .map(|c| c.self_modification.canary_timeout)\n429\t            .unwrap_or(1800);\n430\t\n431\t        let runner = CanaryRunner::new(home.clone(), canary_workspace, canary_timeout);\n432\t\n433\t        let report = runner.run().context(\"canary validation failed\")?;\n434\t\n435\t        if !report.suite_passed {\n436\t            // Canary failed - reject the testing binary\n437\t            runner\n438\t                .reject()\n439\t                .context(\"failed to reject testing binary after canary failure\")?;\n440\t\n441\t            anyhow::bail!(\n442\t                \"canary validation failed: {}/{} tests passed. \\\n443\t                 The testing binary has been rejected. \\\n444\t                 Run 'needle canary --status' for details.\",\n445\t                report.passed,\n446\t                report.total_tests\n447\t            );\n448\t        }\n449\t\n450\t        println!(\n451\t            \"Canary validation passed: {}/{} tests passed.\",\n452\t            report.passed, report.total_tests\n453\t        );\n454\t\n455\t        // Promote :testing to :stable\n456\t        runner\n457\t            .promote()\n458\t            .context(\"failed to promote testing binary to stable\")?;\n459\t        println!(\"Promoted to :stable\");\n460\t    } else {\n461\t        println!(\n462\t            \"No canary workspace found at {}. Installing without validation.\",\n463\t            canary_workspace.display()\n464\t        );\n465\t        println!(\"WARNING: Skipping canary validation is not recommended for production upgrades.\");\n466\t        println!(\n467\t            \"         Set up a canary workspace at {} to enable validation.\",\n468\t            canary_workspace.display()\n469\t        );\n470\t\n471\t 300);\n474\t\n475\t        // Promote without canary validation (fallback behavior)\n476\t        runner\n477\t            .promote()\n478\t            .context(\"failed to promote testing binary to ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n515\t\n516\t/// Compute the SHA-256 hash of a file, returned as a hex string.\n517\tpub fn file_hash(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {\n518\t    let content = fs::read(path)\n519\t        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read file for hashing: {}\", path.display()))?;\n520\t    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n521\t    hasher.update(&content);\n522\t    let result = hasher.finalize();\n523\t    Ok(hex::encode(result))\n524\t}\n525\t\n526\t/// Result of checking for a new :stable binary.\n527\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n528\tpub enum HotReloadCheck {\n529\t    /// No change detected — current binary matches :stable.\n530\t    NoChange,\n531\t    /// New :stable binary detected with different hash.\n532\t    NewBinaryDetected {\n533\t        /// Hash of the currently running binary.\n534\t        old_hash: String,\n535\t        /// Hash of the new :stable binary.\n536\t        new_hash: String,\n537\t        /// Path to the new :stable binary.\n538\t        stable_path: PathBuf,\n539\t    },\n540\t    /// Current binary has been deleted/unlinked (e.g., mv-replaced while running).\n541\t    /// This is an unconditional signal to re-exec into :stable immediately.\n542\t    CurrentBinaryDeleted {\n543\t        /// Hash of the :stable binary to re-exec into.\n544\t        stable_hash: String,\n545\t        /// Path to the new :stable binary.\n546\t        stable_path: PathBuf,\n547\t    },\n548\t    /// Hot-reload is disabled or :stable binary not found.\n549\t    Skipped { reason: String },\n550\t}\n551\t\n552\t/// Check whether the `:stable` binary differs from the currently running binary.\n553\t///\n554\t/// This is called between LOGGING and SELECTING in the worker loop.\n555\tpub fn check_hot_reload(needle_home: &Path) -> Result<HotReloadCheck> {\n556\t    let stable_path = needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable\");\n557\t\n558\t    if !stable_path.exists() {\n559\t        return Ok(HotReloadCheck::Skipped {\n560\t            reason: \"no :stable binary found\".to_string(),\n561\t        });\n562\t    }\n563\t\n564\t    let current_path = get_current_binary_path()?;\n565\t\n566\t    // Detect deleted/unlinked binary (e.g., mv-replaced while running).\n567\t    // On Linux, /proc/self/exe shows \"... (deleted)\" for unlinked inodes.\n568\t    let is_deleted = current_path\n569\t        .to_str()\n570\t        .map(|s| s.ends_with(\" (deleted)\"))\n571\t        .unwrap_or(false);\n572\t\n573\t    if is_deleted {\n574\t        // Current binary is deleted — force re-exec into :stable immediately.\n575\t        // Don't try to hash the deleted path; it will fail.\n576\t        let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_path)?;\n577\t        tracing::warn!(\n578\t            current_path = %current_path.display(),\n579\t            \"current binary has been deleted/unlinked — forcing hot-reload into :stable\"\n580\t        );\n581\t        return Ok(HotReloadCheck::CurrentBinaryDeleted {\n582\t            stable_hash,\n583\t            stable_path,\n584\t        });\n585\t    }\n586\t\n587\t    let current_hash = file_hash(&current_path)?;\n588\t    let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_path)?;\n589\t\n590\t    if current_hash == stable_hash {\n591\t        Ok(HotReloadCheck::NoChange)\n592\t })\n598\t    }\n599\t}\n600\t\n601\t/// Re-exec into the new `:stable` binary with `--resume` to preserve worker identity.\n602\t///\n603\t/// This function does not return on success — it replaces the current process.\n604\t/// On failure, it returns an error so the worker can continue on the current binary.\n605\t#[cfg(unix)]\n606\tpub async fn re_exec_stable(\n607\t    stable_path: &Path,\n608\t    worker_name: &str,\n609\t    workspace: Option<&Path>,\n610\t    agent: Option<&str>,\n611\t    timeout: Option<u64>,\n612\t) -> Result<()> {\n613\t    let stable_path = stable_path.to_path_buf();\n614\t    let worker_name = worker_name.to_string();\n615\t    let workspace = workspace.map(|p| p.to_path_buf());\n616\t    let agent = agent.map(|a| a.to_string());\n617\t\n618\t    // Retry with ETXTBSY handling - the :stable binary was just written and may be busy\n619\t    let mut child = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child(\n620\t        || {\n621\t            let stable_path = stable_path.clone();\n622\t            let worker_name = worker_name.clone();\n623\t            let workspace = workspace.clone();\n624\t            let agent = agent.clone();\n625\t            async move {\n626\t                let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&stable_path);\n627\t                cmd.arg(\"run\").arg(\"--resume\");\n628\t                cmd.arg(\"--identifier\").arg(&worker_name);\n629\t                cmd.arg(\"--count\").arg(\"1\");\n630\t\n631\t                if let Some(ws) = &workspace {\n632\t                    cmd.arg(\"--workspace\").arg(ws);\n633\t                }\n634\t                if let Some(a) = &agent {\n635\t                    cmd.arg(\"--agent\").arg(a);\n636\t                }\n637\t                if let Some(t) = timeout {\n638\t                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(t.to_string());\n639\t                }\n640\t\n641\t                cmd.spawn()\n642\t            }\n643\t        },\n644\t        5,  // max_attempts\n645\t        20, // backoff_ms\n646\t    )\n647\t    .await\n648\t    .context(\"failed to spawn :stable binary after retries\")?;\n649\t\n650\t    // Wait for the child process to complete - it will replace us\n651\t    let status = child\n652\t        .wait()\n653\t        .await\n654\t        .context(\"failed to wait for :stable binary\")?;\n655\t\n656\t    // If we get here, the child exited (which shouldn't happen on successful exec)\n657\t    Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n658\t        \"re-exec failed: :stable binary exited with status {}\",\n659\t        status\n660\t    ))\n661\t}\n662\t\n663\t#[cfg(not(unix))]\n664\tpub async fn re_exec_stable(\n665\t    _stable_path: &Path,\n666\t    _worker_name: &str,\n667\t    _workspace: Option<&Path>,\n668\t PathBuf};\n\nuse anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};\nuse serde::Deserialize;\nuse sha2::{Digest, Sha256};\n\nuse crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child;\n\n/// Current version of the needle binary.\nconst CURRENT_VERSION: &str = env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\");\n\n/// GitHub repository for releases.\nconst GITHUB_REPO: &str = \"jedarden/NEEDLE\";\n\n/// GitHub API URL for latest release.\nfn latest_release_url() -> String {\n    format!(\"https://api.github.com/repos/{GITHUB_REPO}/releases/latest\")\n}\n\n/// Download URL for a specific asset.\nfn asset_download_url(asset_name: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\n        \"https://github.com/{}/releases/latest/download/{}\",\n        GITHUB_REPO, asset_name\n    )\n}\n\n/// GitHub release asset information (fields required for JSON deserialization).\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nstruct ReleaseAsset {\n    name: String,\n    browser_download_url: String,\n}\n\n/// GitHub release information (fields required for JSON deserialization).\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nstruct ReleaseInfo {\n    tag_name: String,\n    name: Option<String>,\n    body: Option<String>,\n    assets: Vec<ReleaseAsset>,\n}\n\n/// Result of checking for updates.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct UpdateCheck {\n    /// Current version.\n    pub current_version: String,\n    /// Latest available version.\n    pub latest_version: String,\n    /// Whether an update is available.\n    pub update_available: bool,\n    /// Release notes (if any).\n    pub release_notes: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Result of downloading to the testing channel.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DownloadToTestingResult {\n    /// Download completed successfully.\n    Downloaded {\n        /// Version that was downloaded.\n        version: String,\n        /// Path to the testing binary.\n        testing_path: PathBuf,\n    },\n    /// Download was skipped because an unpromoted testing binary already exists.\n    Skipped {\n        /// Reason for skipping.\n        reason: String,\n        /// Path to the existing testing binary.\n        testing_path: PathBuf,\n    },\n    /// No update available (already at latest version).\n    NoUpdateAvailable,\n}\n\n/// Check GitHub for the latest release.\n///\n/// Returns information about the latest release compared to the current version.\npub fn check_for_update() -> Result<UpdateCheck> {\n    let response = ureq::agent()\n        .get(&latest_release_url())\n        .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{CURRENT_VERSION}\"))\n        .call()\n        .context(\"failed to fetch latest release from GitHub\")?;\n\n    if response.status() >= 400 {\n        bail!(\n            \"GitHub API returned status {} when checking for updates\",\n            response.status()\n        );\n    }\n\n    let release: ReleaseInfo = serde_json::from_reader(response.into_reader())\n        .context(\"failed to parse GitHub release response\")?;\n\n    // Parse version from tag (strip 'v' prefix if present).\n    let latest_version = release\n        .tag_name\n        .strip_prefix('v')\n        .unwrap_or(&release.tag_name)\n        .to_string();\n\n    let update_available = is_newer_version(&latest_version, CURRENT_VERSION);\n\n    Ok(UpdateCheck {\n        current_version: CURRENT_VERSION.to_string(),\n        latest_version,\n        update_available,\n        release_notes: release.body,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Download a newer GitHub release to the testing channel.\n///\n/// This function downloads the latest release to `needle_home/bin/needle-testing`\n/// instead of overwriting the running binary. It skips download if an unpromoted\n/// testing binary already exists to avoid clobbering an in-flight self-modification\n/// candidate.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// - `Ok(Downloaded)` if download succeeded\n/// - `Ok(Skipped)` if an unpromoted testing binary already exists\n/// - `Ok(NoUpdateAvailable)` if already at latest version\n/// - `Err` if download failed\npub fn download_to_testing_channel() -> Result<DownloadToTestingResult> {\n    let check = check_for_update()?;\n\n    if !check.update_available {\n        return Ok(DownloadToTestingResult::NoUpdateAvailable);\n    }\n\n    let home = needle_home();\n    let bin_dir = home.join(\"bin\");\n    fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n    let testing_binary = bin_dir.join(\"needle-testing\");\n    let stable_binary = bin_dir.join(\"needle-stable\");\n\n    // Check if an unpromoted testing binary already exists.\n    // An unpromoted testing binary is one whose hash differs from :stable.\n    if testing_binary.exists() {\n        let testing_hash = file_hash(&testing_binary);\n        let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_binary);\n\n        // If both exist and have different hashes, testing is unpromoted.\n        if let (Ok(th), Ok(sh)) = (testing_hash, stable_hash) {\n            if th != sh {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    testing_path = %testing_binary.display(),\n                    testing_hash = %th,\n                    stable_hash = %sh,\n                    \"Unpromoted testing binary already exists - skipping download\"\n                );\n                return Ok(DownloadToTestingResult::Skipped {\n                    reason: \"unpromoted testing binary already exists\".to_string(),\n                    testing_path: testing_binary,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Download the new version to testing channel.\n    let asset_name = get_asset_name()?;\n    let download_url = asset_download_url(&asset_name);\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        version = %check.latest_version,\n        url = %download_url,\n        \"Downloading new release to testing channel\"\n    );\n\n    let response = ureq::agent()\n        .get(&download_url)\n        .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{}\", check.current_version))\n        .call()\n        .context(\"failed to download new binary\")?;\n\n    if response.status() >= 400 {\n        bail!(\"download failed with status {}\", response.status());\n    }\n\n    // Read the response into memory.\n    let mut content = Vec::new();\n    response\n        .into_reader()\n        .read_to_end(&mut content)\n        .context(\"failed to read downloaded content\")?;\n\n    // Write the new binary to :testing channel.\n    let temp_path = testing_binary.with_extension(\"tmp\");\n    {\n        let mut file =\n            fs::File::create(&temp_path).context(\"failed to create testing binary file\")?;\n        let mut cursor = Cursor::new(&content);\n        io::copy(&mut cursor, &mut file).context(\"failed to write testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    // Make it executable.\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n        fs::set_permissions(&temp_path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755))\n            .context(\"failed to set executable permissions on testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    // Atomic rename to final testing path.\n    fs::rename(&temp_path, &testing_binary)\n        .context(\"failed to move testing binary to final path\")?;\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        version = %check.latest_version,\n        testing_path = %testing_binary.display(),\n        \"Successfully downloaded to testing channel\"\n    );\n\n    Ok(DownloadToTestingResult::Downloaded {\n        version: check.latest_version,\n        testing_path: testing_binary,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Compare two semver versions, return true if `latest` > `current`.\nfn is_newer_version(latest: &str, current: &str) -> bool {\n    let parse_version =\n        |v: &str| -> Vec<u32> { v.split('.').filter_map(|s| s.parse().ok()).collect() };\n\n    let latest_parts = parse_version(latest);\n    let current_parts = parse_version(current);\n\n    for (l, c) in latest_parts.iter().zip(current_parts.iter()) {\n        if l > c {\n            return true;\n        }\n        if l < c {\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    latest_parts.len() > current_parts.len()\n}\n\n/// Get the platform-specific suffix for release asset names (e.g. \"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\").\nfn get_platform_suffix() -> Result<&'static str> {\n    let os = env::consts::OS;\n    let arch = env::consts::ARCH;\n\n    let suffix = match (os, arch) {\n        (\"linux\", \"x86_64\") => \"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\",\n        (\"linux\", \"aarch64\") => \"aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu\",\n        (\"macos\", \"x86_64\") => \"x86_64-apple-darwin\",\n        (\"macos\", \"aarch64\") => \"aarch64-apple-darwin\",\n        _ => bail!(\"unsupported platform: {os} {arch}\"),\n    };\n\n    Ok(suffix)\n}\n\n/// Get the asset name for the current platform.\nfn get_asset_name() -> Result<String> {\n    Ok(format!(\"needle-{}\", get_platform_suffix()?))\n}\n\n/// Transform binaries shipped alongside needle.\nconst TRANSFORM_BINARIES: &[&str] = &[\"needle-transform-claude\", \"needle-transform-codex\"];\n\n/// Download and install transform binaries next to the needle binary.\n///\n/// Missing assets are skipped with a warning — the main upgrade is not aborted.\n/// After upgrade, `needle doctor` will report any transform that is not on PATH.\nfn install_transform_binaries(install_dir: &Path, platform_suffix: &str) {\n    for transform in TRANSFORM_BINARIES {\n        let asset_name = format!(\"{transform}-{platform_suffix}\");\n        let url = asset_download_url(&asset_name);\n        let dest = install_dir.join(transform);\n\n        println!(\"Installing {transform}...\");\n\n        let response = match ureq::agent()\n            .get(&url)\n            .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{CURRENT_VERSION}\"))\n            .call()\n        {\n            Ok(r) if r.status() < 400 => r,\n            Ok(r) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"  Warning: {transform} not in release (HTTP {}), skipping.\",\n                    r.status()\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                println!(\"  Warning: failed to download {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n                continue;\n            }\n        };\n\n        let mut content = Vec::new();\n        if let Err(e) = response.into_reader().read_to_end(&mut content) {\n            println!(\"  Warning: failed to read {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        let temp_path = dest.with_extension(\"tmp\");\n        if let Err(e) = fs::write(&temp_path, &content) {\n            println!(\n                \"  Warning: failed to write {transform} to {}: {e}. Skipping.\",\n                temp_path.display()\n            );\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        {\n            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n            if let Err(e) = fs::set_permissions(&temp_path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)) {\n                println!(\"  Warning: failed to chmod {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n                let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp_path);\n                continue;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Err(e) = fs::rename(&temp_path, &dest) {\n            println!(\"  Warning: failed to install {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n            let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp_path);\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        println!(\"  {transform} installed to {}.\", dest.display());\n    }\n}\n\n/// Download and install the latest version of needle.\n///\n/// Returns the path to the new binary.\npub fn perform_upgrade() -> Result<PathBuf> {\n    let check = check_for_update()?;\n\n    if !check.update_available {\n        println!(\"Already up to date (version {})\", check.current_version);\n        return get_current_binary_path();\n    }\n\n    println!(\n        \"Upgrading from {} to {}...\",\n        check.current_version, check.latest_version\n    );\n\n    let asset_name = get_asset_name()?;\n    let download_url = asset_download_url(&asset_name);\n\n    println!(\"Downloading from {download_url}...\");\n\n    // Download the new binary.\n    let response = ureq::agent()\n        .get(&download_url)\n        .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{}\", check.current_version))\n        .call()\n        .context(\"failed to download new binary\")?;\n\n    if response.status() >= 400 {\n        bail!(\"download failed with status {}\", response.status());\n    }\n\n    // Read the response into memory.\n    let mut content = Vec::new();\n    response\n        .into_reader()\n        .read_to_end(&mut content)\n        .context(\"failed to read downloaded content\")?;\n\n    // Write the new binary to :testing channel for canary validation.\n    let home = needle_home();\n    let bin_dir = home.join(\"bin\");\n    fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n    let testing_binary = bin_dir.join(\"needle-testing\");\n\n    // Write the new binary to :testing.\n    let mut cursor = Cursor::new(&content);\n    {\n        let mut file =\n            fs::File::create(&testing_binary).context(\"failed to create testing binary file\")?;\n        io::copy(&mut cursor, &mut file).context(\"failed to write testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    // Make it executable.\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n        fs::set_permissions(&testing_binary, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755))\n            .context(\"failed to set executable permissions on testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    println!(\n        \"Downloaded version {} to {}\",\n        check.latest_version,\n        testing_binary.display()\n    );\n\n    // Run canary validation if canary workspace exists.\n    let canary_workspace = home.join(\"canary\");\n    if canary_workspace.exists() {\n        println!(\"Running canary validation...\");\n\n        use crate::canary::CanaryRunner;\n\n        // Honour `self_modification.canary_timeout` instead of hardcoding 300s.\n        // A canary test dispatches a real agent against a real bead, which\n        // routinely takes longer than five minutes — so the hardcoded budget\n        // failed every test by timeout regardless of the binary's health. On\n        // 2026-08-07 that produced \"0/4 tests passed\" for a build whose workers\n        // were observably fine, and rejected it. A gate that cannot pass is not\n        // a gate; it is an outage with a good reputation.\n        let canary_timeout = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_global()\n            .map(|c| c.self_modification.canary_timeout)\n            .unwrap_or(1800);\n\n        let runner = CanaryRunner::new(home.clone(), canary_workspace, canary_timeout);\n\n        let report = runner.run().context(\"canary validation failed\")?;\n\n        if !report.suite_passed {\n            // Canary failed - reject the testing binary\n            runner\n                .reject()\n                .context(\"failed to reject testing binary after canary failure\")?;\n\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"canary validation failed: {}/{} tests passed. \\\n                 The testing binary has been rejected. \\\n                 Run 'needle canary --status' for details.\",\n                report.passed,\n                report.total_tests\n            );\n        }\n\n        println!(\n            \"Canary validation passed: {}/{} tests passed.\",\n            report.passed, report.total_tests\n        );\n\n        // Promote :testing to :stable\n        runner\n            .promote()\n            .context(\"failed to promote testing binary to stable\")?;\n        println!(\"Promoted to :stable\");\n    } else {\n        println!(\n            \"No canary workspace found at {}. Installing without validation.\",\n            canary_workspace.display()\n        );\n        println!(\"WARNING: Skipping canary validation is not recommended for production upgrades.\");\n        println!(\n            \"         Set up a canary workspace at {} to enable validation.\",\n            canary_workspace.display()\n        );\n\n        // Create a minimal canary runner for promotion only (no tests run)\n        use crate::canary::CanaryRunner;\n        let runner = CanaryRunner::new(home.clone(), canary_workspace, 300);\n\n        // Promote without canary validation (fallback behavior)\n        runner\n            .promote()\n            .context(\"failed to promote testing binary to stable\")?;\n        println!(\"Promoted to :stable (without canary validation)\");\n    }\n\n    println!(\"Successfully upgraded to version {}!\", check.latest_version);\n\n    // Install companion transform binaries to the same directory as needle.\n    let stable_path = bin_dir.join(\"needle-stable\");\n    let install_dir = bin_dir.as_path();\n    if let Ok(suffix) = get_platform_suffix() {\n        install_transform_binaries(install_dir, suffix);\n    }\n\n    if let Some(notes) = &check.release_notes {\n        println!(\"\\nRelease notes:\\n{}\", notes);\n    }\n\n    Ok(stable_path)\n}\n\n/// Get the path to the current binary.\nfn get_current_binary_path() -> Result<PathBuf> {\n    env::current_exe().context(\"failed to determine current binary path\")\n}\n\n/// Resolve the needle home directory (~/.needle).\nfn needle_home() -> PathBuf {\n    if let Some(home) = env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n        PathBuf::from(home).join(\".needle\")\n    } else {\n        PathBuf::from(\"/tmp\").join(\".needle\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Hot-reload support\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Compute the SHA-256 hash of a file, returned as a hex string.\npub fn file_hash(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {\n    let content = fs::read(path)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read file for hashing: {}\", path.display()))?;\n    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n    hasher.update(&content);\n    let result = hasher.finalize();\n    Ok(hex::encode(result))\n}\n\n/// Result of checking for a new :stable binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HotReloadCheck {\n    /// No change detected — current binary matches :stable.\n    NoChange,\n    /// New :stable binary detected with different hash.\n    NewBinaryDetected {\n        /// Hash of the currently running binary.\n        old_hash: String,\n        /// Hash of the new :stable binary.\n        new_hash: String,\n        /// Path to the new :stable binary.\n        stable_path: PathBuf,\n    },\n    /// Current binary has been deleted/unlinked (e.g., mv-replaced while running).\n    /// This is an unconditional signal to re-exec into :stable immediately.\n    CurrentBinaryDeleted {\n        /// Hash of the :stable binary to re-exec into.\n        stable_hash: String,\n        /// Path to the new :stable binary.\n        stable_path: PathBuf,\n    },\n    /// Hot-reload is disabled or :stable binary not found.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n}\n\n/// Check whether the `:stable` binary differs from the currently running binary.\n///\n/// This is called between LOGGING and SELECTING in the worker loop.\npub fn check_hot_reload(needle_home: &Path) -> Result<HotReloadCheck> {\n    let stable_path = needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable\");\n\n    if !stable_path.exists() {\n        return Ok(HotReloadCheck::Skipped {\n            reason: \"no :stable binary found\".to_string(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    let current_path = get_current_binary_path()?;\n\n    // Detect deleted/unlinked binary (e.g., mv-replaced while running).\n    // On Linux, /proc/self/exe shows \"... (deleted)\" for unlinked inodes.\n    let is_deleted = current_path\n        .to_str()\n        .map(|s| s.ends_with(\" (deleted)\"))\n        .unwrap_or(false);\n\n    if is_deleted {\n        // Current binary is deleted — force re-exec into :stable immediately.\n        // Don't try to hash the deleted path; it will fail.\n        let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_path)?;\n        tracing::warn!(\n            current_path = %current_path.display(),\n            \"current binary has been deleted/unlinked — forcing hot-reload into :stable\"\n        );\n        return Ok(HotReloadCheck::CurrentBinaryDeleted {\n            stable_hash,\n            stable_path,\n        });\n    }\n\n    let current_hash = file_hash(&current_path)?;\n    let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_path)?;\n\n    if current_hash == stable_hash {\n        Ok(HotReloadCheck::NoChange)\n    } else {\n        Ok(HotReloadCheck::NewBinaryDetected {\n            old_hash: current_hash,\n            new_hash: stable_hash,\n            stable_path,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-exec into the new `:stable` binary with `--resume` to preserve worker identity.\n///\n/// This function does not return on success — it replaces the current process.\n/// On failure, it returns an error so the worker can continue on the current binary.\n#[cfg(unix)]\npub async fn re_exec_stable(\n    stable_path: &Path,\n    worker_name: &str,\n    workspace: Option<&Path>,\n    agent: Option<&str>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let stable_path = stable_path.to_path_buf();\n    let worker_name = worker_name.to_string();\n    let workspace = workspace.map(|p| p.to_path_buf());\n    let agent = agent.map(|a| a.to_string());\n\n    // Retry with ETXTBSY handling - the :stable binary was just written and may be busy\n    let mut child = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child(\n        || {\n            let stable_path = stable_path.clone();\n            let worker_name = worker_name.clone();\n            let workspace = workspace.clone();\n            let agent = agent.clone();\n            async move {\n                let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&stable_path);\n                cmd.arg(\"run\").arg(\"--resume\");\n                cmd.arg(\"--identifier\").arg(&worker_name);\n                cmd.arg(\"--count\").arg(\"1\");\n\n                if let Some(ws) = &workspace {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--workspace\").arg(ws);\n                }\n                if let Some(a) = &agent {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--agent\").arg(a);\n                }\n                if let Some(t) = timeout {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(t.to_string());\n                }\n\n                cmd.spawn()\n            }\n        },\n        5,  // max_attempts\n        20, // backoff_ms\n    )\n    .await\n    .context(\"failed to spawn :stable binary after retries\")?;\n\n    // Wait for the child process to complete - it will replace us\n    let status = child\n        .wait()\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to wait for :stable binary\")?;\n\n    // If we get here, the child exited (which shouldn't happen on successful exec)\n    Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n        \"re-exec failed: :stable binary exited with status {}\",\n        status\n    ))\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\npub async fn re_exec_stable(\n    _stable_path: &Path,\n    _worker_name: &str,\n    _workspace: Option<&Path>,\n    _agent: Option<&str>,\n    _timeout: Option<u64>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    bail!(\"hot-reload re-exec is only supported on Unix platforms\")\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResumeState — state loaded from heartbeat + registry for hot-reload resume\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// State loaded from heartbeat file and registry for worker resumption after\n/// hot-reload. Used by the `--resume` CLI flag to restore worker context.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResumeState {\n    pub worker_id: String,\n    pub beads_processed: u64,\n    pub session: String,\n}\n\nimpl ResumeState {\n    /// Load resume state from heartbeat file and registry.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if no valid heartbeat or registry entry exists for the\n    /// given worker ID. The `worker_id` parameter is the bare NATO name; the\n    /// qualified identity is derived from `config.agent.default` + `worker_id`.\n    pub fn load(config: &crate::config::Config, worker_id: &str) -> Result<Option<Self>> {\n        let heartbeat_dir = config.workspace.home.join(\"state\").join(\"heartbeats\");\n        let qualified_id = format!(\"{}-{}\", config.agent.default, worker_id);\n        let heartbeat_path = heartbeat_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", qualified_id));\n\n        if !heartbeat_path.exists() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %heartbeat_path.display(),\n                \"no heartbeat file for resume\"\n            );\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n\n        let heartbeat_content = fs::read_to_string(&heartbeat_path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read heartbeat: {}\", heartbeat_path.display()))?;\n        let heartbeat: crate::health::HeartbeatData = serde_json::from_str(&heartbeat_content)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse heartbeat: {}\", heartbeat_path.display()))?;\n\n        // Check registry for additional context.\n        let registry = crate::registry::Registry::default_location(&config.workspace.home);\n        let workers = registry.list().context(\"failed to list registry\")?;\n        let entry = workers.iter().find(|w| w.id == qualified_id);\n\n        let beads_processed = match entry {\n            Some(e) => e.beads_processed,\n            None => heartbeat.beads_processed,\n        };\n\n        Ok(Some(ResumeState {\n            worker_id: heartbeat.worker_id,\n            beads_processed,\n            session: heartbeat.session,\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn is_newer_version_major() {\n        assert!(is_newer_version(\"2.0.0\", \"1.0.0\"));\n        assert!(!is_newer_version(\"1.0.0\", \"2.0.0\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn is_newer_version_minor() {\n        assert!(is_newer_version(\"1.1.0\", \"1.0.0\"));\n        assert!(!is_newer_version(\"1.0.0\", \"1.1.0\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn is_newer_version_patch() {\n        assert!(is_newer_version(\"1.0.1\", \"1.0.0\"));\n        assert!(!is_newer_version(\"1.0.0\", \"1.0.1\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn is_newer_version_equal() .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{CURRENT_VERSION}\"))\n        .call()\n        .context(\"failed to fetch latest release from GitHub\")?;\n\n    if response.status() >= 400 {\n        bail!(\n            \"GitHub API returned status {} when checking for updates\",\n            response.status()\n        );\n    }\n\n    let release: ReleaseInfo = serde_json::from_reader(response.into_reader())\n        .context(\"failed to parse GitHub release response\")?;\n\n    // Parse version from tag (strip 'v' prefix if present).\n    let latest_version = release\n        .tag_name\n        .strip_prefix('v')\n        .unwrap_or(&release.tag_name)\n        .to_string();\n\n    let update_available = is_newer_version(&latest_version, CURRENT_VERSION);\n\n    Ok(UpdateCheck {\n        current_version: CURRENT_VERSION.to_string(),\n        latest_version,\n        update_available,\n        release_notes: release.body,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Classify an upgrade error into a category for telemetry.\nfn classify_upgrade_error(error: &anyhow::Error) -> String {\n    let error_msg = error.to_string().to_lowercase();\n\n    if error_msg.contains(\"network\") || error_msg.contains(\"connection\") || error_msg.contains(\"dns\") {\n        \"network\".to_string()\n    } else if error_msg.contains(\"parse\") || error_msg.contains(\"json\") {\n        \"parse\".to_string()\n    } else if error_msg.contains(\"github\") || error_msg.contains(\"api\") || error_msg.contains(\"status\") {\n        \"api\".to_string()\n    } else {\n        \"unknown\".to_string()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Download a newer GitHub release to the testing channel.\n///\n/// This function downloads the latest release to `needle_home/bin/needle-testing`\n/// instead of overwriting the running binary. It skips download if an unpromoted\n/// testing binary already exists to avoid clobbering an in-flight self-modification\n/// candidate.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// - `Ok(Downloaded)` if download succeeded\n/// - `Ok(Skipped)` if an unpromoted testing binary already exists\n/// - `Ok(NoUpdateAvailable)` if already at latest version\n/// - `Err` if download failed\npub fn download_to_testing_channel() -> Result<DownloadToTestingResult> {\n    let check = check_for_update()?;\n\n    if !check.update_available {\n        return Ok(DownloadToTestingResult::NoUpdateAvailable);\n    }\n\n    let home = needle_home();\n    let bin_dir = home.join(\"bin\");\n    fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n    let testing_binary = bin_dir.join(\"needle-testing\");\n    let stable_binary = bin_dir.join(\"needle-stable\");\n\n    // Check if an unpromoted testing binary already exists.\n    // An unpromoted testing binary is one whose hash differs from :stable.\n    if testing_binary.exists() {\n        let testing_hash = file_hash(&testing_binary);\n        let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_binary);\n\n        // If both exist and have different hashes, testing is unpromoted.\n        if let (Ok(th), Ok(sh)) = (testing_hash, stable_hash) {\n            if th != sh {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    testing_path = %testing_binary.display(),\n                    testing_hash = %th,\n                    stable_hash = %sh,\n                    \"Unpromoted testing binary already exists - skipping download\"\n                );\n                return Ok(DownloadToTestingResult::Skipped {\n                    reason: \"unpromoted testing binary already exists\".to_string(),\n                    testing_path: testing_binary,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Download the new version to testing channel.\n    let asset_name = get_asset_name()?;\n    let download_url = asset_download_url(&asset_name);\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        version = %check.latest_version,\n        url = %download_url,\n        \"Downloading new release to testing channel\"\n    );\n\n    let response = ureq::agent()\n        .get(&download_url)\n        .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{}\", check.current_version))\n        .call()\n        .context(\"failed to download new binary\")?;\n\n    if response.status() >= 400 {\n        bail!(\"download failed with status {}\", response.status());\n    }\n\n    // Read the response into memory.\n    let mut content = Vec::new();\n    response\n        .into_reader()\n        .read_to_end(&mut content)\n        .context(\"failed to read downloaded content\")?;\n\n    // Write the new binary to :testing channel.\n    let temp_path = testing_binary.with_extension(\"tmp\");\n    {\n        let mut file =\n            fs::File::create(&temp_path).context(\"failed to create testing binary file\")?;\n        let mut cursor = Cursor::new(&content);\n        io::copy(&mut cursor, &mut file).context(\"failed to write testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    // Make it executable.\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n        fs::set_permissions(&temp_path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755))\n            .context(\"failed to set executable permissions on testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    // Atomic rename to final testing path.\n    fs::rename(&temp_path, &testing_binary)\n        .context(\"failed to move testing binary to final path\")?;\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        version = %check.latest_version,\n        testing_path = %testing_binary.display(),\n        \"Successfully downloaded to testing channel\"\n    );\n\n    Ok(DownloadToTestingResult::Downloaded {\n        version: check.latest_version,\n        testing_path: testing_binary,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Compare two semver versions, return true if `latest` > `current`.\nfn is_newer_version(latest: &str, current: &str) -> bool {\n    let parse_version =\n        |v: &str| -> Vec<u32> { v.split('.').filter_map(|s| s.parse().ok()).collect() };\n\n    let latest_parts = parse_version(latest);\n    let current_parts = parse_version(current);\n\n    for (l, c) in latest_parts.iter().zip(current_parts.iter()) {\n        if l > c {\n            return true;\n        }\n        if l < c {\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    latest_parts.len() > current_parts.len()\n}\n\n/// Get the platform-specific suffix for release asset names (e.g. \"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\").\nfn get_platform_suffix() -> Result<&'static str> {\n    let os = env::consts::OS;\n    let arch = env::consts::ARCH;\n\n    let suffix = match (os, arch) {\n        (\"linux\", \"x86_64\") => \"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\",\n        (\"linux\", \"aarch64\") => \"aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu\",\n        (\"macos\", \"x86_64\") => \"x86_64-apple-darwin\",\n        (\"macos\", \"aarch64\") => \"aarch64-apple-darwin\",\n        _ => bail!(\"unsupported platform: {os} {arch}\"),\n    };\n\n    Ok(suffix)\n}\n\n/// Get the asset name for the current platform.\nfn get_asset_name() -> Result<String> {\n    Ok(format!(\"needle-{}\", get_platform_suffix()?))\n}\n\n/// Transform binaries shipped alongside needle.\nconst TRANSFORM_BINARIES: &[&str] = &[\"needle-transform-claude\", \"needle-transform-codex\"];\n\n/// Download and install transform binaries next to the needle binary.\n///\n/// Missing assets are skipped with a warning — the main upgrade is not aborted.\n/// After upgrade, `needle doctor` will report any transform that is not on PATH.\nfn install_transform_binaries(install_dir: &Path, platform_suffix: &str) {\n    for transform in TRANSFORM_BINARIES {\n        let asset_name = format!(\"{transform}-{platform_suffix}\");\n        let url = asset_download_url(&asset_name);\n        let dest = install_dir.join(transform);\n\n        println!(\"Installing {transform}...\");\n\n        let response = match ureq::agent()\n            .get(&url)\n            .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{CURRENT_VERSION}\"))\n            .call()\n        {\n            Ok(r) if r.status() < 400 => r,\n            Ok(r) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"  Warning: {transform} not in release (HTTP {}), skipping.\",\n                    r.status()\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                println!(\"  Warning: failed to download {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n                continue;\n            }\n        };\n\n        let mut content = Vec::new();\n        if let Err(e) = response.into_reader().read_to_end(&mut content) {\n            println!(\"  Warning: failed to read {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        let temp_path = dest.with_extension(\"tmp\");\n        if let Err(e) = fs::write(&temp_path, &content) {\n            println!(\n                \"  Warning: failed to write {transform} to {}: {e}. Skipping.\",\n                temp_path.display()\n            );\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        {\n            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n            if let Err(e) = fs::set_permissions(&temp_path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)) {\n                println!(\"  Warning: failed to chmod {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n                let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp_path);\n                continue;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Err(e) = fs::rename(&temp_path, &dest) {\n            println!(\"  Warning: failed to install {transform}: {e}. Skipping.\");\n            let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp_path);\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        println!(\"  {transform} installed to {}.\", dest.display());\n    }\n}\n\n/// Download and install the latest version of needle.\n///\n/// Returns the path to the new binary.\npub fn perform_upgrade() -> Result<PathBuf> {\n    let check = check_for_update()?;\n\n    if !check.update_available {\n        println!(\"Already up to date (version {})\", check.current_version);\n        return get_current_binary_path();\n    }\n\n    println!(\n        \"Upgrading from {} to {}...\",\n        check.current_version, check.latest_version\n    );\n\n    let asset_name = get_asset_name()?;\n    let download_url = asset_download_url(&asset_name);\n\n    println!(\"Downloading from {download_url}...\");\n\n    // Download the new binary.\n    let response = ureq::agent()\n        .get(&download_url)\n        .set(\"User-Agent\", &format!(\"needle/{}\", check.current_version))\n        .call()\n        .context(\"failed to download new binary\")?;\n\n    if response.status() >= 400 {\n        bail!(\"download failed with status {}\", response.status());\n    }\n\n    // Read the response into memory.\n    let mut content = Vec::new();\n    response\n        .into_reader()\n        .read_to_end(&mut content)\n        .context(\"failed to read downloaded content\")?;\n\n    // Write the new binary to :testing channel for canary validation.\n    let home = needle_home();\n    let bin_dir = home.join(\"bin\");\n    fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n    let testing_binary = bin_dir.join(\"needle-testing\");\n\n    // Write the new binary to :testing.\n    let mut cursor = Cursor::new(&content);\n    {\n        let mut file =\n            fs::File::create(&testing_binary).context(\"failed to create testing binary file\")?;\n        io::copy(&mut cursor, &mut file).context(\"failed to write testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    // Make it executable.\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n        fs::set_permissions(&testing_binary, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755))\n            .context(\"failed to set executable permissions on testing binary\")?;\n    }\n\n    println!(\n        \"Downloaded version {} to {}\",\n        check.latest_version,\n        testing_binary.display()\n    );\n\n    // Run canary validation if canary workspace exists.\n    let canary_workspace = home.join(\"canary\");\n    if canary_workspace.exists() {\n        println!(\"Running canary validation...\");\n\n        use crate::canary::CanaryRunner;\n\n        // Honour `self_modification.canary_timeout` instead of hardcoding 300s.\n        // A canary test dispatches a real agent against a real bead, which\n        // routinely takes longer than five minutes — so the hardcoded budget\n        // failed every test by timeout regardless of the binary's health. On\n        // 2026-08-07 that produced \"0/4 tests passed\" for a build whose workers\n        // were observably fine, and rejected it. A gate that cannot pass is not\n        // a gate; it is an outage with a good reputation.\n        let canary_timeout = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_global()\n            .map(|c| c.self_modification.canary_timeout)\n            .unwrap_or(1800);\n\n        let runner = CanaryRunner::new(home.clone(), canary_workspace, canary_timeout);\n\n        let report = runner.run().context(\"canary validation failed\")?;\n\n        if !report.suite_passed {\n            // Canary failed - reject the testing binary\n            runner\n                .reject()\n                .context(\"failed to reject testing binary after canary failure\")?;\n\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"canary validation failed: {}/{} tests passed. \\\n                 The testing binary has been rejected. \\\n                 Run 'needle canary --status' for details.\",\n                report.passed,\n                report.total_tests\n            );\n        }\n\n        println!(\n            \"Canary validation passed: {}/{} tests passed.\",\n            report.passed, report.total_tests\n        );\n\n        // Promote :testing to :stable\n        runner\n            .promote()\n            .context(\"failed to promote testing binary to stable\")?;\n        println!(\"Promoted to :stable\");\n    } else {\n        println!(\n            \"No canary workspace found at {}. Installing without validation.\",\n            canary_workspace.display()\n        );\n        println!(\"WARNING: Skipping canary validation is not recommended for production upgrades.\");\n        println!(\n            \"         Set up a canary workspace at {} to enable validation.\",\n            canary_workspace.display()\n        );\n\n        // Create a minimal canary runner for promotion only (no tests run)\n        use crate::canary::CanaryRunner;\n        let runner = CanaryRunner::new(home.clone(), canary_workspace, 300);\n\n        // Promote without canary validation (fallback behavior)\n        runner\n            .promote()\n            .context(\"failed to promote testing binary to stable\")?;\n        println!(\"Promoted to :stable (without canary validation)\");\n    }\n\n    println!(\"Successfully upgraded to version {}!\", check.latest_version);\n\n    // Install companion transform binaries to the same directory as needle.\n    let stable_path = bin_dir.join(\"needle-stable\");\n    let install_dir = bin_dir.as_path();\n    if let Ok(suffix) = get_platform_suffix() {\n        install_transform_binaries(install_dir, suffix);\n    }\n\n    if let Some(notes) = &check.release_notes {\n        println!(\"\\nRelease notes:\\n{}\", notes);\n    }\n\n    Ok(stable_path)\n}\n\n/// Get the path to the current binary.\nfn get_current_binary_path() -> Result<PathBuf> {\n    env::current_exe().context(\"failed to determine current binary path\")\n}\n\n/// Resolve the needle home directory (~/.needle).\nfn needle_home() -> PathBuf {\n    if let Some(home) = env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n        PathBuf::from(home).join(\".needle\")\n    } else {\n        PathBuf::from(\"/tmp\").join(\".needle\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Hot-reload support\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Compute the SHA-256 hash of a file, returned as a hex string.\npub fn file_hash(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {\n    let content = fs::read(path)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read file for hashing: {}\", path.display()))?;\n    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n    hasher.update(&content);\n    let result = hasher.finalize();\n    Ok(hex::encode(result))\n}\n\n/// Result of checking for a new :stable binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HotReloadCheck {\n    /// No change detected — current binary matches :stable.\n    NoChange,\n    /// New :stable binary detected with different hash.\n    NewBinaryDetected {\n        /// Hash of the currently running binary.\n        old_hash: String,\n        /// Hash of the new :stable binary.\n        new_hash: String,\n        /// Path to the new :stable binary.\n        stable_path: PathBuf,\n    },\n    /// Current binary has been deleted/unlinked (e.g., mv-replaced while running).\n    /// This is an unconditional signal to re-exec into :stable immediately.\n    CurrentBinaryDeleted {\n        /// Hash of the :stable binary to re-exec into.\n        stable_hash: String,\n        /// Path to the new :stable binary.\n        stable_path: PathBuf,\n    },\n    /// Hot-reload is disabled or :stable binary not found.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n}\n\n/// Check whether the `:stable` binary differs from the currently running binary.\n///\n/// This is called between LOGGING and SELECTING in the worker loop.\npub fn check_hot_reload(needle_home: &Path) -> Result<HotReloadCheck> {\n    let stable_path = needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable\");\n\n    if !stable_path.exists() {\n        return Ok(HotReloadCheck::Skipped {\n            reason: \"no :stable binary found\".to_string(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    let current_path = get_current_binary_path()?;\n\n    // Detect deleted/unlinked binary (e.g., mv-replaced while running).\n    // On Linux, /proc/self/exe shows \"... (deleted)\" for unlinked inodes.\n    let is_deleted = current_path\n        .to_str()\n        .map(|s| s.ends_with(\" (deleted)\"))\n        .unwrap_or(false);\n\n    if is_deleted {\n        // Current binary is deleted — force re-exec into :stable immediately.\n        // Don't try to hash the deleted path; it will fail.\n        let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_path)?;\n        tracing::warn!(\n            current_path = %current_path.display(),\n            \"current binary has been deleted/unlinked — forcing hot-reload into :stable\"\n        );\n        return Ok(HotReloadCheck::CurrentBinaryDeleted {\n            stable_hash,\n            stable_path,\n        });\n    }\n\n    let current_hash = file_hash(&current_path)?;\n    let stable_hash = file_hash(&stable_path)?;\n\n    if current_hash == stable_hash {\n        Ok(HotReloadCheck::NoChange)\n    } else {\n        Ok(HotReloadCheck::NewBinaryDetected {\n            old_hash: current_hash,\n            new_hash: stable_hash,\n            stable_path,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Re-exec into the new `:stable` binary with `--resume` to preserve worker identity.\n///\n/// This function does not return on success — it replaces the current process.\n/// On failure, it returns an error so the worker can continue on the current binary.\n#[cfg(unix)]\npub async fn re_exec_stable(\n    stable_path: &Path,\n    worker_name: &str,\n    workspace: Option<&Path>,\n    agent: Option<&str>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let stable_path = stable_path.to_path_buf();\n    let worker_name = worker_name.to_string();\n    let workspace = workspace.map(|p| p.to_path_buf());\n    let agent = agent.map(|a| a.to_string());\n\n    // Retry with ETXTBSY handling - the :stable binary was just written and may be busy\n    let mut child = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child(\n        || {\n            let stable_path = stable_path.clone();\n            let worker_name = worker_name.clone();\n            let workspace = workspace.clone();\n            let agent = agent.clone();\n            async move {\n                let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&stable_path);\n                cmd.arg(\"run\").arg(\"--resume\");\n                cmd.arg(\"--identifier\").arg(&worker_name);\n                cmd.arg(\"--count\").arg(\"1\");\n\n                if let Some(ws) = &workspace {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--workspace\").arg(ws);\n                }\n                if let Some(a) = &agent {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--agent\").arg(a);\n                }\n                if let Some(t) = timeout {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(t.to_string());\n                }\n\n                cmd.spawn()\n            }\n        },\n        5,  // max_attempts\n        20, // backoff_ms\n    )\n    .await\n    .context(\"failed to spawn :stable binary after retries\")?;\n\n    // Wait for the child process to complete - it will replace us\n    let status = child\n        .wait()\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to wait for :stable binary\")?;\n\n    // If we get here, the child exited (which shouldn't happen on successful exec)\n    Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n        \"re-exec failed: :stable binary exited with status {}\",\n        status\n    ))\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\npub async fn re_exec_stable(\n    _stable_path: &Path,\n    _worker_name: &str,\n    _workspace: Option<&Path>,\n    _agent: Option<&str>,\n    _timeout: Option<u64>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    bail!(\"hot-reload re-exec is only supported on Unix platforms\")\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResumeState — state loaded from heartbeat + registry for hot-reload resume\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// State loaded from heartbeat file and registry for worker resumption after\n/// hot-reload. Used by the `--resume` CLI flag to restore worker context.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResumeState {\n    pub worker_id: String,\n    pub beads_processed: u64,\n    pub session: String,\n}\n\nimpl ResumeState {\n    /// Load resume state from heartbeat file and registry.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if no valid heartbeat or registry entry exists for the\n    /// given worker ID. The `worker_id` parameter is the bare NATO name; the\n    /// qualified identity is derived from `config.agent.default` + `worker_id`.\n    pub fn load(config: &crate::config::Config, worker_id: &str) -> Result<Option<Self>> {\n        let heartbeat_dir = config.workspace.home.join(\"state\").join(\"heartbeats\");\n        let qualified_id = format!(\"{}-{}\", config.agent.default, worker_id);\n        let heartbeat_path = heartbeat_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", qualified_id));\n\n        if !heartbeat_path.exists() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %heartbeat_path.display(),\n                \"no heartbeat file for resume\"\n            );\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n\n        let heartbeat_content = fs::read_to_string(&heartbeat_path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read heartbeat: {}\", heartbeat_path.display()))?;\n        let heartbeat: crate::health::HeartbeatData = serde_json::from_str(&heartbeat_content)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse heartbeat: {}\", heartbeat_path.display()))?;\n\n        // Check registry for additional context.\n        let registry = crate::registry::Registry::default_location(&config.workspace.home);\n        let workers = registry.list().context(\"failed to list registry\")?;\n        let entry = workers.iter().find(|w| w.id == qualified_id);\n\n        let beads_processed = match entry {\n            Some(e) => e.beads_processed,\n            None => heartbeat.beads_processed,\n        };\n\n        Ok(Some(ResumeState {\n            worker_id: heartbeat.worker_id,\n            beads_processed,\n            session: heartbeat.session,\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n
